newsitem.title: UK: Med to Asia fuel arbitrage draws product eastwards.
newsitem.headline: Med to Asia fuel arbitrage draws product eastwards.

text.p: Strong Asian fuel oil prices are drawing product out of the Mediterranean helping to shorten recent length.

Fuel oil traders and shipping brokers estimated upwards of 250,000 tonnes of fuel has been worked for eastwards trips since the beginning of March. The vast majority is destined for Singapore, although some tankers will discharge in Fujairah, the premier bunker port in the Gulf.
Singapore 380 centistoke material was trading around $92.50 fob on Friday compared with 3.5 percent sulphur fuel in the Mediterranean where prices are close to $76 fob Med.
On an 80,000 tonner going from the Mediterranean to Singapore freight costs are about $12.50 a tonne, shipbrokers said.
A similar sized vessel heading to Fujairah would cost about $6.50 a tonne.
